data_representation.version_1: Feature vectors for both drugs and patients (no graph structure for drugs)
data_representation.version_2: Graph neural network for ligands (atoms + bonds) + MLP for pockets

architecture_paradigm.version_1: Vector-to-vector processing with quantum/classical mixing layer
architecture_paradigm.version_2: Graph-to-vector + Vector-to-vector with quantum/classical interaction layer

optimization_focus.version_1: Speed-optimized for overnight runs (reduced data, fewer layers)

feature_extraction.graph_structure: Bipartite graph (drug-patient edges) but only features are used

version_1_drug_patient.data_format: Flattened feature vectors stored in pandas DataFrame
version_1_drug_patient.negative_sampling: Automatic generation to balance dataset (50% positive, 50% negative)

version_2_ligand_pocket.data_source: PDB protein descriptor files (same source, different processing)

feature_extraction.ligand_features: 10-dimensional atom features + graph structure (bonds as edges)
feature_extraction.graph_structure: True graph representation for ligands with nodes (atoms) and edges (bonds)
feature_extraction.batching: Custom collate function for graph batching

version_2_ligand_pocket.data_format: Graph objects with node features and edge indices
version_2_ligand_pocket.negative_sampling: Automatic generation to balance dataset (50% positive, 50% negative)

data_processing.key_difference: Version 1 treats drugs as feature vectors; Version 2 treats ligands as molecular graphs with explicit atom-bond structure

classical_version.layers: Linear(256→128) → ReLU → Dropout(0.3) → Linear(128→64) → ReLU → Linear(64→1)

version_1_drug_patient.forward_pass: drug_features → drug_encoder → latent_drug [128] | patient_features → patient_encoder → latent_patient [128] | concat → [256] → quantum/classical layer → output [1]

components.name: ligand_encoder
components.description: Processes molecular graph structure (atoms as nodes, bonds as edges)

version_2_ligand_pocket.forward_pass: ligand_graph → GCN encoder → latent_ligand [64] | pocket_features → MLP encoder → latent_pocket [64] | concat → [128] → quantum/classical layer → output [1]

model_architecture.key_architectural_difference: Version 1 uses MLPs for both inputs (vector→vector). Version 2 uses GCN for ligands (graph→vector) and MLP for pockets (vector→vector). Version 2 explicitly models molecular structure.

differences.learning_rates: v1 uses different LRs for quantum (0.005) vs classical (0.0005); v2 uses same LR (0.001) for both
differences.optimizer: v1 uses AdamW with weight decay; v2 uses standard Adam
differences.loss: v1 uses BCEWithLogitsLoss (logits input); v2 uses BCELoss (probability input)
differences.quantum_backend: v1 uses GPU-accelerated quantum simulation; v2 uses CPU simulation
differences.dataset_size: v1 has 11,622 training samples; v2 has 35,968 training samples (3x larger)

key_differences.entanglement: v1 uses StronglyEntanglingLayers (more expressive, more parameters); v2 uses BasicEntanglerLayers (simpler)
key_differences.measurement: v1 measures single qubit; v2 measures all qubits
key_differences.hardware_acceleration: v1 uses GPU quantum simulation; v2 uses CPU
key_differences.expressivity: v1 likely has higher quantum expressivity due to stronger entanglement

comparison.quantum_vs_classical: Incomplete - only quantum model training shown

comparison.quantum_issues: Poor convergence (peaked early at epoch 4), lower expressivity
comparison.classical_advantages: Better convergence, higher precision, more stable training

overall_assessment.version_1: Optimized for speed but incomplete comparison results
overall_assessment.quantum_performance: Version 2 quantum model underperformed, possibly due to CPU simulation, simpler entanglement, or task mismatch

version_1.progress_tracking: Detailed with tqdm progress bars for batches and epochs
version_1.logging: Comprehensive logging with timestamps and performance metrics
version_1.optimization_indicators: Clear indicators of speed optimization (reduced data, reduced layers)
version_1.debugging_support: Verbose logging levels, batch time tracking

version_2.data_handling: Custom collate function for graph batching

code_quality_and_practices.comparison: Both have good practices; v2 has more rigorous reproducibility settings and better visualization

version_1.parallelization: No multiprocessing (NUM_WORKERS=0 to avoid quantum circuit pickling)
version_1.optimization_strategy: Reduced dataset size and model complexity for overnight completion

version_2.gpu_usage: CUDA for neural networks, CPU for quantum simulation
version_2.estimated_runtime: Not specified (likely longer due to 3x dataset size)
version_2.memory_requirements: Higher (3000 samples, 36K training samples, graph structures)

computational_requirements.key_difference: v1 is speed-optimized; v2 is accuracy-optimized with larger dataset

version_1_drug_patient.prediction_task: Will a drug work for a specific patient?
version_1_drug_patient.real_world_application: Predicting drug efficacy for patients, clinical trial matching

version_2_ligand_pocket.prediction_task: Will a small molecule bind to a protein pocket?
version_2_ligand_pocket.input_interpretation: Molecular structure of ligand + Protein pocket features
version_2_ligand_pocket.real_world_application: Virtual screening, lead optimization, structure-based drug design

use_cases_and_applications.domain_difference: v1 is higher-level (drug-patient matching); v2 is molecular-level (ligand-protein binding)

version_1_strengths: Stronger entanglement in quantum circuit (more expressive)
Different learning rates for quantum vs classical (better optimization)
version_1_weaknesses: Loses molecular structure information (treats drugs as vectors)
version_2_strengths: True graph representation preserves molecular structure
version_2_weaknesses: Same learning rate for both models (less flexible optimization)

when_to_use_version_1: Speed is critical (need results in 8-10 hours)
When GPU quantum simulation is available
when_to_use_version_2: Need to preserve molecular structure information
When molecular graphs are important for the task
improvements_for_version_1: Add graph structure for drugs if molecular data is available
improvements_for_version_2: Optimize learning rates separately for quantum vs classical
Investigate why quantum model converged so early

summary.version_1: Speed-optimized drug-patient QGNN using feature vectors and GPU-accelerated quantum simulation. Designed for overnight runs with reduced complexity. Incomplete results shown.
summary.version_2: Full-scale ligand-pocket QGNN using graph neural networks for molecular structure. Complete comparison showing classical model outperforming quantum by 10.24% AUC. CPU quantum simulation.
summary.main_difference: v1 treats drugs as vectors; v2 treats ligands as molecular graphs. v1 is speed-optimized; v2 is completeness-optimized.
summary.quantum_performance: v1: Unknown (incomplete). v2: Underperformed classical significantly (0.67 vs 0.77 AUC).
summary.which_is_better: Depends on use case. v1 for speed and simplicity; v2 for molecular-level accuracy and complete baselines. Both show quantum GNNs need further development to match classical performance.
